current_text.html: When a member of a particular church has willfully neglected the church for a period of one year, or has made it known that he has no intention of fulfilling the church vows, then the Session, continuing to exercise pastoral discipline (BCO 27-1a and 27-4) in the spirit of Galatians 6:1, shall remind the member, if possible both in person and in writing, of the declarations and promises by which he entered into a solemn covenant with God and His Church (BCO 57-5, nos. 3-5), and warn him that, if he persists, his name shall be erased from the roll. If after diligently pursuing such pastoral discipline, and after further inquiry and due delay, the Session is of the judgment that the member will not fulfill his membership obligations in this or any other branch of the Visible Church (cf. BCO 2-2), then the Session shall erase his name from the roll. This erasure is an act of pastoral discipline (BCO 27-1a) without process. The Session shall notify the person, if possible, whose name has been removed. Notwithstanding the above, if a member thus warned makes a written request for process (i.e., BCO Chapters 31-33, 35-36), the Session shall grant such a request. Further, if the Session determines that any offense of such a member is of the nature that process is necessary, the Session may institute such process.

metadata.synopsis: South Florida Presbytery deposed a Teaching Elder, suspended him from the sacraments, and later excommunicated him without first assigning him to a particular church under BCO 46-8. The complainant argued that omission stripped Presbytery of jurisdiction. The SJC denied the complaint: BCO 46-8 requires assignment but fixes no timeframe or mechanism; a deposed minister remains under Presbytery's jurisdiction until transfer, and BCO 37-9(a) preserves censure authority. Deferring under BCO 39-3, the SJC found no clear error in Presbytery's efforts. Two concurrences agreed in result but disputed the majority's broad reasoning and deference.

metadata.synopsis: A member removed from the rolls under BCO 38-4 challenged Presbytery's ruling that she lacked standing to complain because she was no longer a member. The SJC sustained the complaint: standing under BCO 43-1 cannot be defeated by the very removal challenged. Removal under BCO 38-4 is pastoral discipline, a disciplinary case, not a merely administrative act. The SJC remanded to Presbytery to consider the complaint and take the action it should have taken—remand to the Session. The merits of the removal were not decided.

metadata.synopsis: In a BCO 40-5 matter, the SJC held that a presbytery erred in upholding a session's erasure of a member who pled not guilty to failing to submit and pursued divorce. The session wrongly equated declining divorce counsel with refusing submission, failed to assess membership duties in another branch, failed to notify her of erasure, and proceeded without process after dropping charges. The SJC sustained the challenge, directed the session to note the notice failure and remove her under BCO 38-3(a), but ordered no express reversal.

metadata.synopsis: After her session erased her from the roll, Anna Lewis filed a BCO 40-5 report directly with the SJC, alleging the Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley failed to redress the session's alleged failure to give BCO 38-4 notice. The SJC held the filing out of order: under RAO 16-10.c and OMSJC Chapter 15, BCO Chapter 40 matters come to it only by General Assembly referral. It did not decide the merits, but noted that without proper notice Lewis remains a member unless she joined another church. Dissents disputed that limitation and cited past direct reviews.

metadata.synopsis: Kirk Lyons filed BCO 32-2 charges against TE Craig Bulkeley with Western Carolina Presbytery. WCP dismissed the charges, then ruled Lyons's complaint administratively out of order for lack of standing. The SJC answered that the dismissal was not erroneous—Presbytery had discretion under BCO 31-8, 34-2, and 32-20, and the record showed no clear error—but that WCP erred on standing because Lyons's filing brought him under its jurisdiction. Because that error was not prejudicial, the SJC denied the complaint.

metadata.synopsis: Chastain appealed Heritage Presbytery’s 2006 excommunication and deposition. The SJC held the appeal judicially out of order because Chastain had renounced PCA jurisdiction on May 8, 2006. Consequently, Presbytery’s later proceedings were moot and SJC 2005-1 remained in effect. The SJC did not reach the merits. A concurrence questioned the discipline process after renunciation; a dissent argued the majority lacked constitutional authority to recognize unilateral withdrawal and thereby undercut discipline.

relationships.title: Brian Abshire v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Abshire challenged Presbytery’s commission for its appointment, scope, exhortation, summary disposition of two elders’ complaint, and other actions. The SJC sustained only the challenge to deciding the elders’ complaint without BCO 43 procedures and remanded that complaint. It denied the other issues: the commission could conduct the required investigation, the scope objection was untimely, and its exhortation and report were pastoral rather than formal discipline. A separate sixth issue remained before Presbytery and was not decided.

metadata.synopsis: A church member challenged Pacific Northwest Presbytery's denial of her complaint that Faith Presbyterian Church (Tacoma) Session had banned her from worship and sought to erase her membership retroactively under BCO 38-4. The SJC sustained the complaint. Because she never joined Covenant PCA, BCO 46-3 left her membership under Faith's Session; the Session's proposed retroactive erasure did not comply with BCO 38-4's pastoral-oversight steps. The Presbytery therefore erred and should have remanded the matter to the Session. No separate merits relief beyond that remand directive appears.
